literal: Envy called one sinner, wealth having destroyed, evil place having driven will leave.
translation: The sinner called envy will destroy a person's wealth and drive them into a place of evil.
modern: அழுக்காறு என்று சொல்லப்படும் பாவி, ஒருவனுடைய செல்வத்தை அழித்து, அவனைத் துன்பமான இடத்தில் கொண்டுபோய் தள்ளிவிடும்.
explanation: The couplet personifies envy as an unparalleled sinner ('பாவி'). This destructive force acts directly against the envious person by first destroying their present wealth and prosperity ('திருச் செற்று'). Finally, it drives them into a place of evil or suffering ('தீயுழி'). The word 'தீ' can mean fire or evil, but here it describes a state of ruin where envy ultimately leads its host.
